## 1. Dataset Description

For this project, I’m going to use about 800 words from the beginning of *El monte de las ánimas*, a Spanish story by Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer. I’ll start with “La noche de difuntos me despertó” and stop at the end of the sentence closest to 800 words.

I found the story on Project Gutenberg in the collection *Obras escogidas*:

- https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/53552

**Format:** Gutenberg already has a plain-text version of the book:

- https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/53552/pg53552.txt

I’ll copy my selected passage into a `.txt` file, leaving out the book information and section headings. The passage is entirely in Spanish.

**Copyright:** The work is public domain in the United States, so I can include the passage in my public GitHub repository.

## 2. Rationale

I chose this story because I’m interested in Spanish and want to connect this project to something I'm so passionate about which is Spanish. I want to look at which words come up the most, especially words related to nighttime, fear, and sounds.

I’m also curious about how the writer uses the preterite and imperfect. We practice these tenses in class, and it is good for me to comstantly be remembered about grammar so I want to see how they’re used in an actual story instead of separate practice sentences.

## 3. Type of Analysis

- **Frequency and vocabulary:** I’ll count words and find the most common content words, such as nouns, verbs, and adjectives. I’ll separate these from function words, like articles and prepositions. I’ll also calculate the type-token ratio, which compares the number of different words to the total number of words.
- **Grammatical analysis:** I’ll look at preterite and imperfect verb forms, compare how often they appear, and examine how they’re used in the story.

My **units of analysis** will be individual words and verb forms. I’ll keep the original spelling in the raw text and explain any spelling changes I make later.

## 4. Preliminary Questions

1. **Which five content words appear most often in the passage?**
2. **Are there more preterite or imperfect verb forms in the passage?**
3. **Does the writer use the preterite mainly for completed events and the imperfect for background descriptions or ongoing actions?**

I expect the preterite to describe completed events and the imperfect to give background information because that’s how we’ve learned the difference in Spanish classes. I want to see whether this pattern shows up in the passage. My results will describe this sample rather than Spanish stories in general.

## 5. A Look at the Data

Here are eight lines copied from the original plain-text file:

```
La noche de difuntos me despertó á no sé qué hora el doble de las
campanas; su tañido monótono y eterno me trajo á las mientes esta
tradición que oí hace poco en Soria.

Intenté dormir de nuevo; ¡imposible! Una vez aguijoneada, la
imaginación es un caballo que se desboca y al que no sirve tirarle de
la rienda. Por pasar el rato me decidí á escribirla, como en efecto
lo hice.
```
